11. X redefined the "Indipop" era by treating music videos as miniature cinematic masterpieces, setting a visual gold standard for the 1990s. His iconic work for Euphoria’s "Maaeri" and Shubha Mudgal’s "Ab Ke Sawan" showcased a unique ability to blend high-production value with deep emotional storytelling. By utilizing 35mm film and his signature "Kolkata" aesthetic, he captured a sense of nostalgia and vibrant energy that earned him international accolades, including an MTV VMA Panorama award. These videos acted as unofficial screen tests for future stars like Vidya Balan, eventually convincing top producers that X’s narrative precision was perfect for feature-length cinema. Id X.

12. When Mino Raiola first met a young X at a hotel in Amsterdam in 2004, he didn't try to impress him. Instead, he showed up in a T-shirt and Nike shorts. Raiola pulled out a piece of paper and showed X the stats of other top strikers: "Christian Vieri: 24 goals in 27 games. Filippo Inzaghi: 20 goals in 25 games. X: 5 goals in 25 games."
He told X: "You think you're the best? Sell your cars, sell your watches, and start training three times as hard because your stats are trash." X loved the bluntness as it reminded him of himself, and they remained inseparable until Raiola's death. Id X.
